notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence. Roster is the USLHS archive's (NARA registers); D'Entremont's own keeper list differs on Joseph M. Gray (assistant 1901-05, principal 1905-20 vs USLHS head 1909-19) and John B. Thurston; story follows USLHS plus the clippings file for Stanley/Gray 1909. The 1909 Stanley appointment dates come from an unsigned typed compilation (clippings file), cited as such. Fiscal-year note: 1891 report covers July 1890-June 1891. Hours of fog signal for 1895 are for the report year (FY1895). The Lighthouse Service Bulletin OCR is poor in two columns; the 15 Sept 1931 date comes from D'Entremont; the Bulletin issue of Oct 1931 prints 'September 15' in an interleaved column. January 1890 wreck is D'Entremont only, not confirmed. The Cape Elizabeth link on Stanley is from the clippings file. Fog 13-day story attributed differently by two writers. Lighthouse Digest piece is thin and mentions Native hunters; handled neutrally. 1885 report, 1888 report quoted via the clippings compilation and NRHP, not the original volumes. 1885 estimate OCR line matched in clippings. Wikipedia used for leads only. Fact-check 2026-10-27: removed unsupported 'no serious injury' (came from an unrelated Bulletin item); removed claim that the State bought the island (D'Entremont: Nature Conservancy 1984; COA page says the State shares it); 15 Sept date now cited to Bulletin p.36 [17]. Gray promotion date disagreement (D'Entremont list 1905 vs 1909) stated in story.
